report.title: 2025 Annual Water Quality Report - Stanford University Water Resources and Civil Infrastructure (May 2026)

sources_described: All of the current drinking water supply comes from the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS), wholesaled by the SFPUC: surface water stored in reservoirs in the Sierra Nevada (Hetch Hetchy, unfiltered but UV/chlorine disinfected, pH adjusted, fluoridated and chloraminated), Alameda County and San Mateo County, with local Bay Area reservoir water treated at the Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant (page 2). Stanford maintains groundwater wells only as an emergency backup supply (page 6).

violations: Page 9, 'Notification of Process Monitoring Violation': the San Francisco Regional Water System failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23, 2025 to July 2, 2025, because of equipment failure; corrected July 3, 2025; not an emergency and did not impact water quality. Notice provided by Stanford (System 4310013) on behalf of the SFRWS, distributed June 01, 2026.

Page 4-5: highest monthly total coliform positive rate was 6% (standard: no more than 5% of monthly samples). Stanford performed an assessment in January 2025 following a coliform detection; an incorrectly installed service connection was determined to be the cause and was corrected.

Page 5 footnote j: in the 2024 lead and copper tap sampling at 30 homes, one home had an initial lead result above the action level (41 ppb) but a second sample was ND; all other results were below the lead and copper Action Levels. 90th percentiles were < 5 ppb lead and < 50 ppb copper.
Page 1 and footnote a: water quality was in compliance with SWRCB-DDW and USEPA requirements; all results met State and Federal drinking water health standards.
extraction_notes: Single data table on page 5 ('only detected contaminants shown'), one set of values with no per-source columns; rows are marked * (SFPUC regional-system samples) or † (Stanford distribution samples), recorded in notes rather than source_group. The TURBIDITY section is split by source as rows (Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy Water; Filtered Water - SVWTP) and those entries carry the row label in source_group. Lead/copper are from the 2024 tap sampling (footnote j). Two extra entries are not table rows: treated-water fluoride from footnote h and the 2021 PFAS statement from page 6. The PDF filename says 'finaldraft' but the site publishes it as the 2025 CCR. Convention: a range printed 'ND - x' or '<n - x' is stored range_low 0 / range_high x (the printed string is kept in notes). Rows whose Average (or 90th percentile) is printed 'ND' or '<n' but whose range shows a detection are stored value null, average null, detected true, value_basis 'average (printed ND)' - nothing is substituted for the unprintable average. Rows printed ND with no range are detected false. 'sample_year' is the latest year when the report prints a year range; the printed range is in notes.
